feed.headline: Shock of rail tragedy gives way to sorrow and outrage in politically divided Spain
feed.ai: The latest train crash will pile pressure on the government of Pedro Sánchez, one month before the general election.

feed.headline: Carney to push for closer ties at Canada-EU summit in Montreal
feed.ai: The term "associate member" is reportedly off the table as officials discuss deeper economic and defence ties.

feed.headline: Norway and Finland leaders hold rare call with Putin
feed.ai: An end to the conflict in Ukraine "will not be achieved through silence," Finland's President Alexander Stubb said.

feed.headline: Joy and disbelief on Serbian streets as Vučić concedes election defeat
feed.ai: BBC correspondent Nick Thorpe reports from Belgrade, where there were rapturous celebrations following the victory of the student-led movement.

feed.headline: Who actually controls Ukraine's access to Starlink?
feed.ai: President Zelensky says limits to the technology continue to affect Ukrainian forces, while US officials and Elon Musk offer conflicting accounts of who controls it.

feed.headline: Are the French riots a warning of an intense election to come?
feed.ai: Rioting, looting and vandalism has gripped France over the weekend after protests spiralled out of control across the country.

feed.headline: In Marseille, Macron Confronts a Potent Mix of France’s Problems
feed.ai: France’s second city, five years into a presidential development plan, is grappling with the social strains that have fueled protests across the country.

feed.headline: Trump Officials Discussing Sanctions Relief for Russian Fund, Russia Acknowledges
feed.ai: A Russian official said potential relief for a state investment fund was part of talks. Russia has sought to wring economic benefits from the negotiations on ending the war with Ukraine.

feed.headline: Albania: opposition MPs disrupt parliament with smoke flares
feed.ai: Opposition MPs disrupted a parliamentary session in Albania by brandishing smoke flares and displaying photographs of injured protesters. They accused police of using violence against demonstrators demanding Prime Minister Edi Rama's resignation.

feed.headline: Putin calls Elon Musk a 'genius' as Russia builds its own Starlink rival
feed.ai: Russian President Vladimir Putin has praised Elon Musk as a “genius” for deploying thousands of satellites into orbit. Speaking in Moscow, Putin highlighted Russia’s efforts to develop its own satellite internet network to rival Musk’s Starlink.

feed.headline: Europe Today: Second high-speed rail disaster in nine months leaves Spain in grief
feed.ai: At least 68 people died when two high-speed trains collided south of Madrid, Spain's second deadly rail crash this year. In Montreal, EU leaders meet Mark Carney to launch an 'Alliance for the Future'. We also look at next week's US midterms, Ukraine's defence capabilities, and rising oil prices.

feed.headline: Celebrations in Serbia after veteran ruler Vučić loses election to student-led protest movement
feed.ai: The populist right-wing leader of 12 years says it is "clear" his party has lost the vote billed as a referendum on the country's future.
